title.zh: 卷七十四 列傳第四: 耶律敵剌 蕭痕篤 康默記 韓延徽 韓知古
title.en: Volume 74 Biographies 4: Yelu Dila, Xiao Hendu, Kang Moji, Han Yanhui, Han Zhigu
title.raw: 卷七十四 列傳第四: 耶律敵剌 蕭痕篤 康默記 韓延徽 韓知古 Volume 74 Biographies 4: Yelu Dila, Xiao Hendu, Kang Moji, Han Yanhui, Han Zhigu

translations.literal: Yelu Dila, Xiao Hendu, Kang Moji
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Dila, Xiao Hendu, and Kang Moji

translations.literal: (Yanshou) >〉
translations.idiomatic: (Yanshou)]〉

sentences.zh: 韓延徽

translations.literal: Han Yanhui
translations.idiomatic: Han Yanhui

translations.literal: (Deshu, Shaoxun, Shaofang, Zirang) >〉
translations.idiomatic: (Deshu, Shaoxun, Shaofang, and Zirang)]〉

translations.literal: Han Zhigu
translations.idiomatic: Han Zhigu

sentences.zh: （匡嗣德源德凝）〉

translations.literal: (Kuangsai, Deyuan, Dening) >〉
translations.idiomatic: (Kuangsai, Deyuan, and Dening)]〉

sentences.zh: 耶律敵剌，字合魯隱，遙輦鮮質可汗之子。

translations.literal: Yelu Dila, courtesy name Heluyin, was a son of the Jianzhi Khan of the Yaolian clan.
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Dila, whose courtesy name was Heluyin, was a son of the Jianzhi Khan of the Yaolian clan.

sentences.zh: 太祖踐阼，與敞穩海裏同心輔政。

translations.literal: When the Taizu Emperor ascended the throne, he and Changwen Haili assisted in government with one mind.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizu took the throne, he and Changwen Haili worked together in loyal support of the government.

sentences.zh: 太祖知其忠實，命掌禮儀，且諉以軍事。

translations.literal: The Taizu Emperor knew his loyalty and honesty, appointed him to oversee rites and ceremonies, and also entrusted him with military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu recognized his loyalty and integrity, put him in charge of ceremonial matters, and also delegated military affairs to him.

sentences.zh: 後以平內亂功，代轄裏為奚六部吐裏，卒。

translations.literal: Later, for his merit in pacifying internal disorder, he replaced Zaruli as tuli of the Six Xi Tribes, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for his success in quelling internal strife, he succeeded Zaruli as tuli of the Six Xi Tribes and died in office.

sentences.zh: 敵剌善騎射，頗好禮文。

translations.literal: Dila excelled at mounted archery and was quite fond of ritual and literary culture.
translations.idiomatic: Dila was skilled in horsemanship and archery and had a marked taste for ritual and literary learning.

sentences.zh: 蕭痕篤，字兀裏軫，叠剌部人。

translations.literal: Xiao Hendu, courtesy name Wulizhen, was a man of the Diela tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Hendu, whose courtesy name was Wulizhen, came from the Diela tribe.

sentences.zh: 其先相遙輦氏。

translations.literal: His ancestors had served as chancellors to the Yaolian clan.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears had long been chancellors to the Yaolian.

sentences.zh: 痕篤少慷慨，以才能自任。

translations.literal: Hendu was generous and bold in youth and took confidence in his own talent.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Hendu was open-handed and spirited, trusting fully in his own abilities.

sentences.zh: 早隸太祖帳下，數從征討。

translations.literal: Early on he served under the Taizu Emperor's banner and repeatedly followed him on campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Taizu Emperor's service early and took part in many expeditions.

sentences.zh: 既踐阼，除北府宰相。

translations.literal: Once the throne had been taken, he was appointed Northern Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: After the enthronement he was made chancellor of the Northern Administration.

sentences.zh: 痕篤事親孝，為政尚寬簡。

translations.literal: Hendu was filial toward his parents, and in government he favored leniency and simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: Hendu was dutiful to his parents, and his rule favored clemency and restraint.

sentences.zh: 康默記，本名照。

translations.literal: Kang Moji's original name was Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Moji, whose original name was Zhao.

sentences.zh: 少為薊州衙校，太祖侵薊州得之，愛其材，隸麾下。

translations.literal: In youth he was a guard officer of Jizhou; when the Taizu Emperor invaded Jizhou and obtained him, he admired his talent and enrolled him under his banner.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he served as a guard officer in Jizhou. When Emperor Taizu took Jizhou and captured him, he valued his ability and took him into his retinue.

sentences.zh: 一切蕃、漢相涉事，屬默記折衷之，悉合上意。

translations.literal: All matters involving Khitan and Han interrelation were assigned to Mojie to adjudicate, and all accorded with the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Every affair that touched both Khitan and Han he entrusted to Mojie to settle; each decision matched the emperor's wishes.

sentences.zh: 時諸部新附，文法未備，默記推析律意，論決重輕，不差毫厘。

translations.literal: At the time the tribes had newly submitted and statutes were not yet complete; Mojie analyzed the intent of the laws and decided the weight of guilt and leniency, without error by a hair's breadth.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes had only just submitted and the legal code was still incomplete; Mojie parsed the spirit of the statutes and weighed penalties and pardons with flawless precision.

sentences.zh: 罹禁網者，人人自以為不冤。

translations.literal: Those caught in the penal net each considered themselves not wronged.
translations.idiomatic: Those brought before the law all believed themselves treated fairly.

sentences.zh: 頃之，拜左尚書。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was appointed Left Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made Left Minister.

sentences.zh: 神冊三年，始建都，默記董役，人咸勸趨，百日而訖事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shence, when the capital was first established, Mojie supervised the labor; all were urged to press on, and the work was completed in a hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: In Shence year 3, as the capital was first being built, Mojie oversaw construction; workers were driven hard, and the project was finished in a hundred days.

sentences.zh: 五年，為皇都夷離畢。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he became yilü-bi of the imperial capital.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he was made yilü-bi of the imperial capital.

sentences.zh: 會太祖出師居庸關，命默記將漢軍進逼長蘆水寨，俘馘甚眾。

translations.literal: When the Taizu Emperor marched out through Juyong Pass, he ordered Mojie to lead the Han army to press against Changlu Water Fortress; captive heads were very many.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizu took the field through Juyong Pass, he sent Mojie with the Han army against Changlu Water Fortress, taking a great number of prisoners and heads.

sentences.zh: 天贊四年，親征渤海，默記與韓知古從。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianzan, on the personal campaign against Bohai, Mojie followed with Han Zhigu.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianzan year 4 he accompanied the emperor's expedition against Bohai, alongside Han Zhigu.

sentences.zh: 後大諲譔叛，命諸將攻之。

translations.literal: Later Dayinzan rebelled, and the emperor ordered the generals to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Later Dayinzan rose in rebellion, and the emperor ordered his commanders against him.

sentences.zh: 默記分薄東門，率驍勇先登。

translations.literal: Mojie assigned forces to press the east gate and led crack troops in the first ascent.
translations.idiomatic: Mojie pressed the east gate and led elite troops in the assault.

sentences.zh: 既拔，與韓延徽下長嶺府。

translations.literal: Once it was taken, with Han Yanhui he descended on Changling Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After the city fell he joined Han Yanhui in taking Changling Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 軍還，已下城邑多叛，默記與阿古只平之。

translations.literal: When the army returned, many of the cities already taken rebelled; Mojie with Aguozi quelled them.
translations.idiomatic: On the march home many captured towns rebelled; Mojie and Aguozi put them down.

sentences.zh: 既破回跋城，歸營太祖山陵畢，卒。

translations.literal: After breaking Huiba City, he returned to camp, completed the Taizu Emperor's tomb, and died.
translations.idiomatic: After storming Huiba City he returned to camp, finished work on Emperor Taizu's tomb, and died.

sentences.zh: 佐命功臣其一也。

translations.literal: He was one of the merit ministers who assisted in founding the dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: He was numbered among the founding merit ministers.

sentences.zh: 孫延壽，字胤昌，少倜儻，謂其所親：「大丈夫為將，當效節邊垂，馬革裹屍。

translations.literal: His grandson Yanshou, courtesy name Yinchang, was bold and free-spirited in youth; he told those close to him: "A true man who becomes a general should prove his loyalty on the frontier border, wrapped in horsehide for burial."
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Yanshou, whose courtesy name was Yinchang, was dashing from youth. He told his intimates: "A man who takes command should stand his post on the frontier and meet death wrapped in horsehide."

sentences.zh: 」景宗特授千牛衛大將軍。

translations.literal: " Emperor Jingzong specially awarded him general of the Thousand-Ox Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jingzong specially appointed him general of the Thousand-Ox Guard.

sentences.zh: 宋人攻南京，諸將既成列，延壽獨奮擊陣前，敵遂大潰。

translations.literal: When Song forces attacked Nanjing, the generals had already formed ranks; Yanshou alone charged fiercely before the lines, and the enemy thereupon routed in great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song attacked Nanjing and the commanders had drawn up battle lines, Yanshou alone charged the front; the enemy broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 以功遙授保大軍節度使。

translations.literal: For his merit he was remotely appointed military commissioner of the Baoda Army.
translations.idiomatic: For this exploit he received the honorary title of Baoda Army military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 乾亨三年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the third year of Qianheng.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Qianheng year 3.

sentences.zh: 韓延徽，字藏明，幽州安次人。

translations.literal: Han Yanhui, courtesy name Cangming, was a native of Anci in Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yanhui, whose courtesy name was Cangming, came from Anci in Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 父夢殷，累官薊、儒、順三州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Mengyin held successive posts as prefect of Ji, Ru, and Shun.
translations.idiomatic: His father Mengyin had served in turn as prefect of Ji, Ru, and Shun.

sentences.zh: 延徽少英，燕帥劉仁恭奇之，召為幽都府文學、平州錄事參軍，同馮道祗候院，授幽州觀察度支使。

translations.literal: Yanhui was outstanding in youth; the Yan commander Liu Rengong was struck by him and summoned him as literary instructor of the Youdu Prefecture office and recorder-assistant of Pingzhou, attached to the Di-hou Court with Feng Dao; he was appointed Youzhou observation revenue commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: A gifted youth, Yanhui caught the eye of the Yan commander Liu Rengong, who made him literary instructor at the Youdu prefectural office and recorder-assistant of Pingzhou, assigned with Feng Dao to the reception bureau, then Youzhou observation revenue commissioner.

sentences.zh: 後守光為帥，延徽來聘，太祖怒其不屈，留之。

translations.literal: Later, when Shouguang became commander, Yanhui came on a diplomatic mission; the Taizu Emperor was angered that he would not bow and detained him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shouguang later became commander, Yanhui came as envoy; Emperor Taizu, angered that he refused to submit, kept him.

sentences.zh: 述律後諫曰：「彼秉節弗撓，賢者也，奈何困辱之？

translations.literal: Empress Shulü remonstrated: "He holds to his integrity and will not bend—a worthy man. How can we humiliate and abuse him?"
translations.idiomatic: Empress Shulü urged: "He keeps his integrity and will not yield—a worthy man. Why subject him to hardship and shame?"

sentences.zh: 」太祖召與語，合上意，立命參軍事。

translations.literal: " The Taizu Emperor summoned him to converse; it accorded with his intent, and he immediately ordered him to assist in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu summoned him for an audience, was pleased with him, and at once put him on his staff.

sentences.zh: 攻党項、室韋，服諸部落，延徽之籌居多。

translations.literal: In attacking the Tangut and Shiwei and subduing the tribes, Yanhui's planning figured largely.
translations.idiomatic: In campaigns against the Tangut and Shiwei and in bringing the tribes to heel, Yanhui's counsel was decisive.

sentences.zh: 乃請樹城郭，分市裏，以居漢人之降者。

translations.literal: He then requested to erect walls and cities, divide wards and market blocks, and settle surrendering Han there.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed building walled towns with separate wards and markets for surrendered Han settlers.

sentences.zh: 又為定配偶，教墾藝，以生養之。

translations.literal: He also arranged marriages, taught clearing and cultivation, and nourished them for growth.
translations.idiomatic: He arranged marriages, taught farming, and saw to their livelihood.

sentences.zh: 以故逃亡者少。

translations.literal: For this reason fugitives were few.
translations.idiomatic: Consequently few fled.

sentences.zh: 居久之，慨然懷其鄉里，賦詩見意，遂亡歸唐。

translations.literal: After dwelling there long, he sighed with longing for his homeland, composed a poem to express his intent, and thereupon fled and returned to Tang.
translations.idiomatic: After a long stay he yearned for home, wrote a poem to say so, and fled back to Tang.

sentences.zh: 已而與他將王緘有隙，懼及難，乃省親幽州，匿故人王德明舍。

translations.literal: Before long he had a rift with another commander Wang Jian, feared disaster would reach him, and so went to visit family in Youzhou, hiding in the house of his old acquaintance Wang Deming.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he fell out with the general Wang Jian and, fearing reprisal, visited his family in Youzhou and hid with his friend Wang Deming.

sentences.zh: 德明問所適，延徽曰：「吾將復走契丹。

translations.literal: Deming asked where he was bound; Yanhui said: "I intend to flee again to the Khitan."
translations.idiomatic: Deming asked where he was headed. Yanhui said: "I mean to flee back to the Khitan."

sentences.zh: 」德明不以為然。

translations.literal: " Deming did not approve.
translations.idiomatic: Deming thought this unwise.

sentences.zh: 延徽笑曰：「彼失我如失左右手，其見我必喜。

translations.literal: Yanhui smiled and said: "They will lose me as one loses left and right hands; when they see me they are sure to rejoice."
translations.idiomatic: Yanhui smiled: "They will miss me as they would their own hands—when they see me again they will be delighted."

sentences.zh: 」既至，太祖問故。

translations.literal: " When he arrived, the Taizu Emperor asked the reason.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived Emperor Taizu asked why he had come.

sentences.zh: 延徽曰：「忘親非孝，棄君非忠。

translations.literal: Yanhui said: "To forget one's parents is not filial; to abandon one's lord is not loyal."
translations.idiomatic: Yanhui said: "To forget one's parents is unfilial; to abandon one's lord is disloyal."

sentences.zh: 臣雖挺身逃，臣心在陛下。

translations.literal: Although I fled with my person, my heart was with Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Though I fled in body, my heart remained with you.

sentences.zh: 臣是以復來。

translations.literal: Therefore I have come again.
translations.idiomatic: That is why I have returned.

sentences.zh: 」上大悅，賜名曰匣列。

translations.literal: " The emperor was greatly pleased and bestowed the name Xialie.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and gave him the name Xialie.

sentences.zh: 「匣列」，遼言復來也。

translations.literal: "Xialie"—in Liao speech it means "return again."
translations.idiomatic: In Khitan, "Xialie" means "one who comes back."

sentences.zh: 即命為守政事令、崇文館大學士，中外事悉令參決。

translations.literal: He was immediately appointed acting governance director and grand academician of the Chongwen Hall; all internal and external affairs were ordered for him to deliberate and decide.
translations.idiomatic: He was promptly made acting governance director and Chongwen Hall grand academician, with authority over both palace and frontier affairs.

sentences.zh: 天贊四年，從征渤海，大諲譔乞降。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianzan, on the campaign against Bohai, Dayinzan begged to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianzan year 4, on the expedition against Bohai, Dayinzan offered surrender.

sentences.zh: 既而復叛，與諸將破其城，以功拜左僕射。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he rebelled again; with the generals Yanhui stormed his city, and for his merit was appointed Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He soon rebelled again; Yanhui joined the other generals in storming his city and was rewarded with the post of Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 又與康默記攻長嶺府，拔之。

translations.literal: Again with Kang Moji he attacked Changling Prefecture and took it.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Kang Moji in taking Changling Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 師還，太祖崩，哀動左右。

translations.literal: When the army returned, the Taizu Emperor died; grief moved those at his side.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return Emperor Taizu had died; Yanhui grieved so deeply that all around him were moved.

sentences.zh: 太宗朝，封魯國公，仍為政事令。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Taizong he was enfeoffed Duke of Lu and remained governance director.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Taizong he was enfeoffed Duke of Lu and kept his post as governance director.

sentences.zh: 使晉還，改南京三司使。

translations.literal: Returning from a mission to Jin, he was transferred to commissioner of the three bureaus at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: After an embassy to Jin he was made Nanjing commissioner of the three revenue bureaus.

sentences.zh: 世宗朝，遷南府宰相，建政事省，設張理具，稱盡力吏。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Shizong he was promoted to chancellor of the Southern Administration, established the Governance Office, set up filing racks, and was called an official who gave his utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Shizong he rose to Southern chancellor, founded the Governance Office with its document systems, and was praised as an official who spared no effort.

sentences.zh: 天祿五年六月，河東使請行冊禮，帝詔延徽定其制，延徽奏一遵太宗冊晉帝禮，從之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fifth year of Tianlu, the envoy from Hedong requested that investiture rites be performed; the emperor ordered Yanhui to fix the protocol, and Yanhui memorialized that all should follow the Taizong Emperor's rites for investing the Jin emperor, and this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Tianlu year 5 an envoy from Hedong asked that investiture rites be performed; the emperor charged Yanhui to set the protocol, and Yanhui proposed following exactly Emperor Taizong's ceremony for investing the Jin emperor—the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 應歷中，致仕。

translations.literal: During Yingli he retired.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yingli era he retired from office.

sentences.zh: 子德樞鎮東平，詔許每歲東歸省。

translations.literal: His son Deshu garrisoned Dongping; an edict permitted him to return east each year for family visits.
translations.idiomatic: His son Deshu was posted at Dongping; the court allowed him an annual visit home.

sentences.zh: 九年卒，年七十八。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he died, aged seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died in year 9, at seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 上聞震悼，贈尚書令，葬幽州之魯郭，世為崇文令公。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard, he was shaken with grief; he was posthumously granted Director of the Department of State Affairs, buried at Luguo in Youzhou, and his house was known for generations as the Chongwen Duke line.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was stricken with grief and posthumously made him Director of the Department of State Affairs; he was buried at Luguo in Youzhou, and his family was known for generations as the Chongwen Dukes.

sentences.zh: 初，延徽南奔，太祖夢白鶴自帳中出；

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yanhui fled south, the Taizu Emperor dreamed a white crane flew out from the tent;
translations.idiomatic: When Yanhui first fled south, Emperor Taizu dreamed that a white crane flew out of his tent;

sentences.zh: 比還，復入帳中。

translations.literal: when it returned, it re-entered the tent.
translations.idiomatic: when it came back it flew in again.

sentences.zh: 詰旦，謂侍臣曰：「延徽至矣。

translations.literal: At daybreak he told the attending ministers: "Yanhui has arrived."
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he told his attendants: "Yanhui is here."

sentences.zh: 」已而果然。

translations.literal: " And indeed it was so.
translations.idiomatic: And so it proved.

sentences.zh: 太祖初元，庶事草創，凡營都邑，建宮殿，正君臣定，名分，法度井井，延徽力也。

translations.literal: In the founding years of Taizu, when all affairs were in raw beginning, in establishing capital cities, building palaces, rectifying ruler and ministers and fixing names and ranks, with rites and laws in good order—all was Yanhui's effort.
translations.idiomatic: In the dynasty's founding days, when institutions were still being shaped—from planning capitals and palaces to setting proper relations between ruler and ministers and establishing ranks and laws—Yanhui's hand was everywhere.

sentences.zh: 為佐命功臣之一。

translations.literal: He was one of the founding merit ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He ranked among the founding merit ministers.

sentences.zh: 子德樞。

translations.literal: His son Deshu.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Deshu.

sentences.zh: 德樞年甫十五，太宗見之，謂延徽曰：「是兒卿家之福，朕國之寶，真英物也！

translations.literal: Deshu was just fifteen; when Taizong saw him he said to Yanhui: "This boy is the fortune of your house and the treasure of my state—a truly outstanding prodigy!"
translations.idiomatic: Deshu was only fifteen when Emperor Taizong saw him and told Yanhui: "This child is your family's blessing and my realm's treasure—a remarkable youth indeed!"

sentences.zh: 」未冠，守左羽林大將軍，遷特進太尉。

translations.literal: " Before cap and hairpin he held the post of Left General of the Feathered Forest Guard and was promoted to specially advanced Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: Before he came of age he was made Left General of the Feathered Forest Guard, then promoted to specially advanced Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 時漢人降與轉徙者，多寓東平。

translations.literal: At the time many Han who surrendered or were relocated lodged at Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Many surrendered or relocated Han had settled at Dongping.

sentences.zh: 丁歲災，饑饉疾厲。

translations.literal: In a ding year disaster struck: famine and pestilence.
translations.idiomatic: A ding year brought famine and plague.

sentences.zh: 德樞請往撫字之，授遼興軍節度使。

translations.literal: Deshu requested to go comfort and nourish them and was appointed military commissioner of the Liaoxing Army.
translations.idiomatic: Deshu volunteered to go relieve them and was appointed Liaoxing Army military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 下車整紛剔蠹，恩煦信孚，勸農桑，興教化，期月民獲蘇息。

translations.literal: Upon taking office he put chaos in order and removed corruption; kindness warmed and trust was secured; he encouraged farming and sericulture and promoted teaching and transformation; within a month the people recovered and revived.
translations.idiomatic: Taking office he restored order, rooted out abuse, and won the people's trust; he promoted agriculture and education, and within a month the district began to recover.

sentences.zh: 入為南院宣徽使，遙授天平軍節度使，平、灤、營三州管內觀察處置等使，門下平章事。

translations.literal: He entered service as commissioner of the Southern Court Privy Seal and was remotely appointed military commissioner of the Tianping Army, observer and disposal commissioner for Ping, Luan, and Ying, and associate director of the Gate Department.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court as Southern Privy Seal commissioner, he received the honorary titles of Tianping Army military commissioner, supervisory commissioner for Ping, Luan, and Ying, and associate director of the Gate Department.

sentences.zh: 已而加開府儀同三司、行侍中，封趙國公。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was additionally granted Grand Master with opened office and third-rank honors, acting palace attendant, and enfeoffed Duke of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was given the additional titles of Grand Master with opened office equal to the Three Excellencies and acting palace attendant, and was enfeoffed Duke of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 保寧元年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Baoning.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Baoning year 1.

sentences.zh: 孫紹勛、紹芳。

translations.literal: Grandsons Shaoxun and Shaofang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandsons were Shaoxun and Shaofang.

sentences.zh: 紹勛，仕至東京戶部使。

translations.literal: Shaoxun rose in office to commissioner of the household bureau at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoxun rose to household commissioner at the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 會大延琳叛，被執，辭不屈，賊以鋸解之，憤罵至死。

translations.literal: When Dayanlin rebelled he was seized; in interrogation he would not yield; the rebels sawed him apart; he railed in fury until death.
translations.idiomatic: When Dayanlin rebelled he was captured; defiant under interrogation, the rebels dismembered him with saws, and he cursed them to his last breath.

sentences.zh: 紹芳，重熙間參知政事，加兼侍中。

translations.literal: Shaofang, during Chongxi, was appointed assistant administrator of government affairs with the additional title of palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongxi era Shaofang served as vice director of the Secretariat with the additional title of palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 時延議征李元昊，力諫不聽，出為廣德軍節度使。

translations.literal: At the time the court debated campaigning against Li Yuanhao; he remonstrated strongly but was not heeded and was sent out as military commissioner of the Guangde Army.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated war against Li Yuanhao he argued against it without success and was posted as Guangde Army military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 聞敗，嘔血卒。

translations.literal: On hearing of defeat he vomited blood and died.
translations.idiomatic: When news of defeat arrived he spat blood and died.

sentences.zh: 孫資讓，壽隆初拜中書侍郎、平章事。

translations.literal: Grandson Zirang, at the start of Shoulong, was appointed vice director of the Secretariat and associate director.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Zirang was made vice director of the Secretariat and associate director at the opening of the Shoulong era.

sentences.zh: 會宋徽宗嗣位，遣使來報，有司按籍，有「登寶位」文，坐是出為崇義軍節度使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huizong of Song succeeded to the throne and sent envoys to announce it, the relevant offices checked the records and found wording of "ascending the throne"; for this he was demoted to military commissioner of the Chongyi Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Song Huizong succeeded and sent notice, the record-checkers found the phrase "ascending the imperial throne"; Zirang was demoted to Chongyi Army military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 改鎮遼興，卒。

translations.literal: Transferred to garrison Liaoxing, he died.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Liaoxing, he died in office.

sentences.zh: 韓知古，薊州玉田人，善謀有識量。

translations.literal: Han Zhigu, a native of Yutian in Jizhou, was skilled in planning and possessed discernment and breadth.
translations.idiomatic: Han Zhigu, from Yutian in Jizhou, was a skilled strategist of steady judgment.

sentences.zh: 太祖平薊時，知古六歲，為淳欽皇后兄欲穩所得。

translations.literal: When the Taizu Emperor pacified Ji, Zhigu was six years old and was taken by Yuwen, elder brother of Empress Chunqin.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizu took Ji, Zhigu was six; he was taken by Yuwen, elder brother of Empress Chunqin.

sentences.zh: 後來嬪，知古從焉，未得省見。

translations.literal: Later when she entered the harem Zhigu accompanied her but could not obtain an imperial audience.
translations.idiomatic: When she later entered the palace harem Zhigu came with her but never gained audience with the emperor.

sentences.zh: 久之，負其有，怏怏不得志，挺身逃庸保，以供資用。

translations.literal: After long waiting, confident of his worth yet frustrated and unfulfilled, he cast off restraint and fled to hire himself out for wages to supply his needs.
translations.idiomatic: Long unrecognized despite his talents, he grew restless and slipped away to hire himself out for a living.

sentences.zh: 其子匡嗣得親近太祖，因間言。

translations.literal: His son Kuangsi gained closeness to the Taizu Emperor and spoke of him in private.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kuangsi had the emperor's ear and mentioned him in passing.

sentences.zh: 太祖召見與語，賢之，命參謀議。

translations.literal: The Taizu Emperor summoned him, conversed with him, deemed him worthy, and ordered him to assist in planning.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu summoned him, found him capable, and put him on the planning staff.

sentences.zh: 神冊初，遙授彰武軍節度使。

translations.literal: At the start of Shence he was remotely appointed military commissioner of the Zhangwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Shence he received the honorary post of Zhangwu Army military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 久之，信任益篤，總知漢兒司事，兼主諸國禮儀。

translations.literal: After long service trust deepened further; he was put in overall charge of Han affairs and concurrently directed the rites and ceremonies of all domains.
translations.idiomatic: Over time the emperor's trust deepened; he took charge of Han administration and also oversaw ceremonial protocol.

sentences.zh: 時儀法疏闊，知古援據故典，參酌國俗，與漢儀雜就之，使國人易知而行。

translations.literal: At the time ritual law was loose and incomplete; Zhigu drew on old statutes, weighed national custom, and blended them with Han rites so that countrymen would easily understand and put them into practice.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual protocol was still rudimentary; Zhigu drew on ancient precedents, adapted Khitan custom, and blended in Han practice until the people could follow them with ease.

sentences.zh: 頃之，拜左僕射，與康默記將漢軍征渤海有功，遷中書令。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was appointed Left Vice Director; with Kang Moji he led the Han army on the Bohai campaign with merit and was promoted to Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made Left Vice Director; campaigning against Bohai with Kang Moji at the head of the Han army earned him promotion to Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 天顯中卒，為佐命功臣之一。

translations.literal: He died during Tianxian and was one of the founding merit ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the Tianxian era, numbered among the founding merit ministers.

sentences.zh: 子匡嗣。

translations.literal: His son Kuangsi.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Kuangsi.

sentences.zh: 匡嗣以善醫，直長樂宮，皇后視之猶子。

translations.literal: Kuangsi, for skill in medicine, served directly at Changle Palace; the empress regarded him as her own son.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in medicine, Kuangsi served at Changle Palace, where the empress treated him like a son.

sentences.zh: 應歷十年，為太祖廟詳穩。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Yingli he was detailed stable officer of the Taizu Emperor's temple.
translations.idiomatic: In Yingli year 10 he was made temple officer for Emperor Taizu's shrine.

sentences.zh: 後宋王喜隱謀叛，辭引匡嗣，上置不問。

translations.literal: Later when Prince of Song Xiyin plotted rebellion, his testimony implicated Kuangsi; the emperor set the matter aside without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Song Xiyin later plotted rebellion and named Kuangsi in his confession, the emperor took no action.

sentences.zh: 初，景宗在藩邸，善匡嗣。

translations.literal: Early on, when Jingzong was at the princely residence, he was on good terms with Kuangsi.
translations.idiomatic: In his days as heir apparent Emperor Jingzong had been close to Kuangsi.

sentences.zh: 即位，拜上京留守。

translations.literal: Upon accession Kuangsi was appointed defender of the Upper Capital.
translations.idiomatic: When he took the throne he made Kuangsi defender of the Upper Capital.

sentences.zh: 頃之，王燕，改南京留守。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter enfeoffed Prince of Yan, he was changed to defender of Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Soon enfeoffed Prince of Yan, Kuangsi was transferred to Nanjing as defender.

sentences.zh: 保寧末，以留守攝樞密使。

translations.literal: At the end of Baoning, as defender he also acted as commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Baoning he served as defender while also acting as privy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時耶律虎古使宋還，言宋人必取河東，合先事以為備。

translations.literal: At the time Yelü Hugu returned from a mission to Song and said the Song would certainly take Hedong; it was fitting to prepare ahead.
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Hugu, returning from an embassy to Song, warned that the Song would seize Hedong and urged early preparations.

sentences.zh: 匡嗣詆之曰：「寧有是！

translations.literal: Kuangsi denounced him, saying: "How could there be such a thing!"
translations.idiomatic: Kuangsi scoffed: "Nonsense!"

sentences.zh: 」已而宋人果取太原，乘勝逼燕。

translations.literal: " Before long the Song indeed took Taiyuan and, pressing the victory, threatened Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Song took Taiyuan and pressed toward Yan in victory.

sentences.zh: 匡嗣與南府宰相沙、惕隱休哥侵宋，軍於滿城。

translations.literal: Kuangsi with Southern Chancellor Yelu Sha and tithen Xiuge invaded Song and encamped at Mancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangsi joined Southern Chancellor Yelu Sha and tithen Xiuge in an incursion against Song and encamped at Mancheng.

sentences.zh: 方陣，宋人請降。

translations.literal: As battle lines were forming, the Song requested surrender.
translations.idiomatic: As the armies drew up, the Song offered surrender.

sentences.zh: 匡嗣欲納之，休哥曰：「彼軍氣甚銳，疑誘我也。

translations.literal: Kuangsi wished to accept them; Xiuge said: "Their army's spirit is very sharp; I suspect they mean to lure us."
translations.idiomatic: Kuangsi wanted to accept; Xiuge said: "Their morale is too high—they mean to bait us."

sentences.zh: 可整頓士卒以禦。

translations.literal: We should ready the troops to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Ready the men for a stand."

sentences.zh: 」匡嗣不聽。

translations.literal: " Kuangsi did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangsi refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 俄而宋軍鼓噪薄我，眾蹙踐，塵起漲天。

translations.literal: Before long the Song army beat drums and clamored, pressing on us; the masses crowded and trampled; dust rose flooding the sky.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly the Song charged with drums and shouts; our ranks buckled and trampled one another; dust blotted out the sky.

sentences.zh: 匡嗣倉卒諭諸將，無當其鋒。

translations.literal: Kuangsi in haste instructed the generals that none should meet their spearhead.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangsi hurriedly told his commanders not to meet the charge.

sentences.zh: 眾既奔，遇伏兵扼要路，匡嗣棄旗鼓遁，其眾走易州山，獨休哥收所棄兵械，全軍還。

translations.literal: Once the masses had fled they met ambush troops blocking the vital road; Kuangsi cast away banners and drums and fled; his army fled to the mountains of Yizhou; only Xiuge gathered the abandoned weapons and returned with the whole army intact.
translations.idiomatic: As the army broke, ambushers blocked the retreat; Kuangsi abandoned his standards and fled, his troops scattering into the Yizhou hills; only Xiuge recovered the abandoned arms and brought his command safely back.

sentences.zh: 帝怒匡嗣，數之曰：「爾違眾謀，深入敵境，爾罪一也；

translations.literal: The emperor was angry with Kuangsi and reckoned his crimes: "You defied collective counsel and penetrated deep into enemy territory—your first crime;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor raged at Kuangsi and listed his offenses: "You rejected your officers' counsel and drove deep into enemy country—first offense;

sentences.zh: 號令不肅，行伍不整，爾罪二也；

translations.literal: Your orders were lax and ranks disordered—your second crime;
translations.idiomatic: Your orders were lax and ranks disordered—second offense;

sentences.zh: 棄我師旅，挺身鼠竄，爾罪三也；

translations.literal: You abandoned your army and scurried off like a rat—your third crime;
translations.idiomatic: You abandoned your command and scurried off like a rat—third offense;

sentences.zh: 偵候失機，守禦弗備，爾罪四也；

translations.literal: Your scouts failed and defenses were unprepared—your fourth crime;
translations.idiomatic: You failed your scouts and left defenses unprepared—fourth offense;

sentences.zh: 捐棄旗鼓，損威辱國，爾罪五也。

translations.literal: You cast away your banners and disgraced the realm—your fifth crime.
translations.idiomatic: You cast away your banners and disgraced the realm—fifth offense.'

sentences.zh: 」促令誅之。

translations.literal: " He ordered execution at once.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered execution at once.

sentences.zh: 皇后引諸內戚徐為開解，上重違其請。

translations.literal: The empress led the inner kin to intercede gradually and open the matter; the emperor greatly hesitated to go against her plea.
translations.idiomatic: The empress and her kinsmen gradually pleaded for mercy; reluctant to refuse her, the emperor stayed his hand.

sentences.zh: 良久，威稍霽，乃杖而免之。

translations.literal: After a long while his wrath eased slightly, and he had him beaten with the staff and spared.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually his anger cooled and he had Kuangsi beaten and released.

sentences.zh: 既而遙授晉昌軍節度使。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was remotely appointed military commissioner of the Jinchang Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was later given the honorary post of Jinchang Army military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 乾亨三年，改西南面招討使，卒。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qianheng he was changed to Southwest Route pacification commissioner and died.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianheng year 3 he was made Southwest Route pacification commissioner and died.

sentences.zh: 睿智皇后聞之，遣使臨吊，賻贈甚厚，後追贈尚書令。

translations.literal: When the Wise Empress heard, she sent envoys to mourn and gave lavish funeral gifts; later he was posthumously granted Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wise Empress heard, she sent envoys to mourn and gave lavish funeral gifts; later he was posthumously made Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 五子：德源，德讓，後賜名隆運，德威，德崇，德凝。

translations.literal: Five sons: Deyuan; Derang, later granted the name Longyun; Dewei; Dechong; and Dening.
translations.idiomatic: He had five sons: Deyuan; Derang, later granted the name Longyun; Dewei; Dechong; and Dening.

sentences.zh: 德源、德凝附傳，余各有傳。

translations.literal: Deyuan and Dening are treated in appendices here; the others have separate biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Deyuan and Dening are treated in appendices here; the others have separate biographies.

sentences.zh: 德源，性愚而貪，早侍景宗邸。

translations.literal: Deyuan was dull-witted and greedy; he entered the heir apparent Jingzong's service early.
translations.idiomatic: Deyuan was dull-witted and greedy; he entered the heir apparent Jingzong's service early.

sentences.zh: 及即位，列近侍。

translations.literal: When Jingzong took the throne he was ranked among the close attendants.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingzong took the throne he was ranked among the close attendants.

sentences.zh: 保寧間，官崇義、興國二軍節度使，加檢校太師。

translations.literal: During Baoning he held the posts of Chongyi and Xingguo army military commissioner and was made honorary Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: During Baoning he held the posts of Chongyi and Xingguo army military commissioner and was made honorary Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 以賄名，德讓貽書諫之，終不悛。

translations.literal: His reputation for bribery was notorious; Derang wrote urging reform, but he never changed.
translations.idiomatic: His reputation for bribery was notorious; Derang wrote urging reform, but he never changed.

sentences.zh: 以故論者少之。

translations.literal: Critics therefore held him in low regard.
translations.idiomatic: Critics therefore held him in low regard.

sentences.zh: 後加同政事門下平章事，遙攝保寧軍節度使。

translations.literal: Later he was made associate director of the Gate Department and acting Baoning Army military commissioner in absentia.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made associate director of the Gate Department and acting Baoning Army military commissioner in absentia.

sentences.zh: 乾亨初卒。

translations.literal: He died at the start of Qianheng.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the start of Qianheng.

sentences.zh: 德凝，廉遜廉謹。

translations.literal: Dening was modest, yielding, and careful.
translations.idiomatic: Dening was modest, yielding, and careful.

sentences.zh: 保寧中，遷護軍司徒。

translations.literal: During Baoning he was promoted to Guardian Army grand steward.
translations.idiomatic: During Baoning he was promoted to Guardian Army grand steward.

sentences.zh: 開泰中，累遷護衛太保、都宮使、崇義軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the Kaitai era he rose through Guardian Cavalry grand guardian, palace intendant, and Chongyi Army military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaitai era he rose through Guardian Cavalry grand guardian, palace intendant, and Chongyi Army military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 移鎮廣德，秩滿，部民請留，從之。

translations.literal: Transferred to Guangde, at the end of his term the people asked him to stay, and the court agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Guangde, at the end of his term the people asked him to stay, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 改西南面招討使，党項隆益答叛，平之。

translations.literal: Made Southwest Route pacification commissioner, he suppressed the Tangut chief Longyida's rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Made Southwest Route pacification commissioner, he suppressed the Tangut chief Longyida's rebellion.

sentences.zh: 遷大同軍節度使，卒於官。

translations.literal: Promoted to Datong Army military commissioner, he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Datong Army military commissioner, he died in office.

sentences.zh: 子郭三，終天德軍節度使。

translations.literal: His son Guo San ended as Tiande Army military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: His son Guo San ended as Tiande Army military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 孫高家奴，終南院宣徽使；

translations.literal: His grandson Gaojianu became Southern Privy Seal commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Gaojianu became Southern Privy Seal commissioner;

sentences.zh: 高十，終遼興軍節度使。

translations.literal: Gao Shi ended as Liaoxing Army military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Shi ended as Liaoxing Army military commissioner.
